title: Heavy letters: reciting with a full mouth: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y4 lesson 10 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Heavy letters rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 10. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Seven heavy letters
points: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ
Remember them as خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ

head: Not this
This
rows: Rounding the lips to sound heavy: 'qoo-la'
Lift the back of the tongue; lips stay natural: 'qaa-la'

keywords.def: the tongue rising: what makes a letter heavy

questions.q: Say «وَصَدَّقَ» (92:6) and name the heavy letters.
questions.a: ص and ق are heavy; و and د are light.

questions.q: How many heavy letters are always heavy?
Heavy letter hunt (pupil PDF): circle the heavy letters in Al-'Alaq 96:1 to 5. Today's rota group recites 92:1 to 7 to the teacher in turn.
Extend: write the seven heavy letters from memory.
questions.a: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ

questions.q: Stretch: which heavy letter is in «ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ»? Trick question: explain.
questions.a: None: ع and ل are light here (the laam is only heavy in the Name Allah after fathah or dammah).

questions.q: Which of these is a heavy letter?
questions.a: A) ط. ط is one of خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ. ت and ك are light: they are its light partners.

questions.q: Which word has a heavy letter?
Think again: Say 'saad' and then 'seen'. One sounds full and deep, one sounds thin. Which is which, and what did your tongue do?
questions.a: Saad (ص) is heavy: the back of the tongue rises and the mouth fills. Seen (س) is light.
